[ASSISTANT_SAID] Musicians earn a small royalty fee for every stream, and while the revenue per stream is low, the massive audience has made up for it.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The focus has shifted from album sales to single releases, allowing musicians to release shorter, more frequent projects.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Music streaming services have created opportunities for independent musicians to distribute their music worldwide without needing a record label.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] While revenue per stream is lower compared to traditional sales, the reach of streaming services has created new opportunities for musicians.  
[USER] User acknowledges the advantages for independent musicians but questions if they are still at a disadvantage compared to those with record label backing.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Independent musicians may still face disadvantages compared to those backed by record labels, which have resources for marketing, promotion, and production.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Record labels have established relationships with playlist curators, influencers, and media outlets, which can help musicians gain wider exposure.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Record labels have more leverage in negotiating royalty rates with streaming services.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Social media and digital content distribution channels have reduced barriers for independent musicians, allowing them to build fan bases without record label support.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The changing landscape of the music industry has created more opportunities for independent musicians despite some disadvantages.
